\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{وصية} (waṣiyya)}{وصية (waṣiyya)}]{\ar{وصية} (waṣiyya) — a will, a testament; advice}

\label{lesson:AR-C337-wasiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a dowry, then the Arabic for the eve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{وصية}}
\textbf{\ar{وصية}} — \emph{waṣiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}a will, a testament; advice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كتب} \ar{الرجل} \ar{وصيته} \ar{قبل} \ar{موته}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kataba ar-rajul waṣiyyatahu qabla mawtihi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man wrote his will before he died.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{وصايا}, \emph{waṣāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{وصية}} (\emph{waṣiyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-ṣ-y} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to enjoin, to give a charge\textquotedblright{}. A \emph{waṣiyya} is the charge a person leaves behind.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waṣiyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waṣiyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kataba ar-rajul waṣiyyatahu qabla mawtihi.} — The man wrote his will before he died.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a dowry, then the Arabic for the eve, then say \emph{waṣiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{وصية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A will, a testament; advice\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ميراث} (mīrāth)}{ميراث (mīrāth)}]{\ar{ميراث} (mīrāth) — an inheritance}

\label{lesson:AR-C337-mirath}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for the eve, then the Arabic for a will.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ميراث}}
\textbf{\ar{ميراث}} — \emph{mīrāth} — \textquotedblleft{}an inheritance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ترك} \ar{الأب} \ar{لأولاده} \ar{ميراثا} \ar{صغيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taraka al-ab li-awlādihi mīrāthan ṣaghīran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The father left his children a small inheritance.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ميراث}} (\emph{mīrāth}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-r-th} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}. The \emph{w} of the root shows as \emph{ī} after the \emph{mi-} of the pattern.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mīrāth}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mīrāth}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taraka al-ab li-awlādihi mīrāthan ṣaghīran.} — The father left his children a small inheritance.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for the eve, then the Arabic for a will, then say \emph{mīrāth} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ميراث} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An inheritance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ورث} (waritha)}{ورث (waritha)}]{\ar{ورث} (waritha) — to inherit}

\label{lesson:AR-C337-waritha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a will, then the Arabic for an inheritance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ورث}}
\textbf{\ar{ورث}} — \emph{waritha} — \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ورثت} \ar{البنت} \ar{بيتا} \ar{من} \ar{جدتها}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{warithat al-bint baytan min jaddatihā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The girl inherited a house from her grandmother.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرث}, \emph{yarith}.

The present drops the \ar{و}: \ar{يرث}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ورث}} (\emph{waritha}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-r-th} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}; \emph{mīrāth} and \emph{turāth} are both what is inherited.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waritha}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waritha}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{warithat al-bint baytan min jaddatihā.} — The girl inherited a house from her grandmother.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a will, then the Arabic for an inheritance, then say \emph{waritha} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ورث} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To inherit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{وارث} (wārith)}{وارث (wārith)}]{\ar{وارث} (wārith) — an heir}

\label{lesson:AR-C337-warith}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an inheritance, then the Arabic for to inherit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{وارث}}
\textbf{\ar{وارث}} — \emph{wārith} — \textquotedblleft{}an heir\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الابن} \ar{الوارث} \ar{الوحيد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-ibn al-wārith al-waḥīd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The son was the only heir.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{ورثة}, \emph{waratha}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{وارث}} (\emph{wārith}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-r-th} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Wārith} is the active participle, \textquotedblleft{}one who inherits\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wārith}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-ibn al-wārith al-waḥīd.} — The son was the only heir.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an inheritance, then the Arabic for to inherit, then say \emph{wārith} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أرملة} (armala)}{أرملة (armala)}]{\ar{أرملة} (armala) — a widow}

\label{lesson:AR-C337-armala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to inherit, then the Arabic for an heir.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أرملة}}
\textbf{\ar{أرملة}} — \emph{armala} — \textquotedblleft{}a widow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عاشت} \ar{الأرملة} \ar{مع} \ar{ابنتها}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿāshat al-armala maʿa ibnatihā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The widow lived with her daughter.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أرامل}, \emph{arāmil}.

A widower is \ar{أرمل}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أرملة}} (\emph{armala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-m-l} (Lane), where Lane gives \emph{armala} as a woman without a husband, and \emph{armal}, a man in need.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{armala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{armala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿāshat al-armala maʿa ibnatihā.} — The widow lived with her daughter.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to inherit, then the Arabic for an heir, then say \emph{armala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أرملة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A widow\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
